disclaimer: NU Map is an independent, student-built planner. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to Northeastern University. Data is scraped from Northeastern's public catalog and refreshed on a schedule; always confirm with the official catalog and an academic advisor.

legend.prereqs: Flat token list: course refs {subject, number, minGrade} joined by 'And'/'Or' strings; nested arrays are parenthesized groups. minGrade is the minimum passing grade required.
legend.coreqs: Courses that must be taken in the same term.
legend.offerings.terms: Past/scheduled terms by Banner code (YYYY = academic-year END year; Fall runs in YYYY-1). sections/enrolled/capacity are snapshots from the scheduled scrape, NOT live seat availability.
legend.offerings.typicalDays: Weekdays on which at least 50% of recent sections met.
legend.offerings.daysPct: Percent of recent sections meeting on each weekday (M/T/W/Th/F).
legend.offerings.meetingPatterns: [pattern, percent-of-sections] pairs; in patterns like 'MWR', R means Thursday.
legend.instructors: Per season. sharePct = average percent of that season's enrolled students taught by this professor (recent terms). 'reviews' links their RateMyHusky page when one exists.
legend.level: undergrad for course numbers below 5000, grad otherwise.
legend.typicallyOffered: Seasons in which the course was scheduled in at least two-thirds of that season's terms on record since it first appeared — a pattern, not a guarantee.
legend.unlocks: Courses that list this course in their prerequisites — what taking it opens up.
legend.nuPath: NUpath general-education attributes this course carries.
legend.repeatable: Whether the course may be taken more than once for credit (repeatMax / repeatMaxSH cap it).

courses.subject: ITLN
courses.title: Elementary Italian 1
courses.description: Designed for students with very little or no prior knowledge of Italian. Provides a lively introduction to basic oral expression, listening comprehension, and elementary reading and writing. Each lesson incorporates helpful information about daily life in Italy and the varied cultures within the world of Italian speakers. Laboratory practice complements class work, enables students to work aloud at their own speed, reinforces their acquisition of essential structures, and acquaints them with a vast library of audio-visual resources.

courses.subject: ITLN
courses.title: Elementary Italian 2
courses.description: Continues ITLN 1101. Reviews and continues the study of grammar and basic language skills. Offers progressively more intensive practice in oral and written communication. Laboratory practice complements class work, enables students to work aloud at their own speed, reinforces their acquisition of essential structures, and acquaints them with a vast library of audio-visual resources.

courses.subject: ITLN
courses.title: Dante’s "Inferno" and Medieval Italian Culture
courses.description: Presents an overview of Dante’s "Commedia," with a focus on the first book, "Inferno." Explores the descending levels of hell, analyzing the historical and cultural context of Dante's time, including political events and social structures. Examines theological concepts such as sin, punishment, redemption, and the afterlife from the perspective of Christian theology. Through the literary analysis of selected chapters (canti), evaluates the potential relevance of the poem to the modern human condition and to the reader's own experiences. Taught in English.

courses.subject: ITLN
courses.title: Realism and Modernism in Italian Film
courses.description: Examines the significance of postwar Italian cinema as a crucial platform for cultural expression by exploring some of the most influential films and directors from the neorealism era to the 1970s. Analyzes neorealism film, considering its role in empowering marginalized groups and reshaping Italy's cinematic landscape. Explores how issues such as class divisions, culture conflicts, and ideological debates are portrayed in films, with the aim of influencing and redefining Italian unity and identity. Investigates the sociocultural repercussions of the economic boom of the 1950s and 1960s, particularly in the transition toward modernism in cinema. Offers students an opportunity to appreciate the aesthetic expressions within Italian cinema and to explore the connection between film styles and practices with their historical and cultural contexts. Conducted in English.

courses.subject: ITLN
courses.title: Introduction to Italian Culture
courses.description: Explores the construction of an Italian national cultural identity through a historical and cross-disciplinary perspective from the Middle Ages; the Renaissance; and the modern, post–WWII period. Organized into modules that focus on the major issues related to the idea of unity and division such as north and south divide, regionalism, language pluralism, fascism and dissent, criminal organizations, and migration. Conducted in English.

courses.subject: ITLN
courses.title: Special Topics in Italian Culture
courses.description: Presents an in-depth exploration of aspects of Italian cultural, social, and intellectual history, which could include literature, philosophy, art, education, politics, gender, and society. Emphasizes critical analysis of primary and secondary sources, historical context, and interdisciplinary perspectives to deepen students’ understanding of Italy's rich heritage and its place within global intellectual discourse. Themes and topics vary. Taught in English. May be repeated twice.

courses.subject: ITLN
courses.title: Advanced Italian 1
courses.description: Stresses the fundamentals of Italian to promote effective self-expression through speaking and writing and to explore the idiomatic aspects of the language. Through progressive class discussions and oral and written commentaries, students analyze a contemporary Italian novel or a Italian cultural reader, screenplay, or collection of short stories. The course strives, first, to help students read and comprehend modern Italian writing with confidence and to be able to talk and write about it in good Italian; and second, to provide preparation for advanced courses.

courses.description: Continues ITLN 3101. Enhances and reinforces language and communication skills that students encounter when they are abroad.
